title: Canonical tree depth lower-bounds decision-tree depth
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction on those variables, and write $f|_\rho$ for the restricted Boolean function $x \mapsto f\big(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x\big)$, which evaluates $f$ on the assignment that takes the fixed value of $\rho$ where one is set and reads the remaining coordinates from $x$. Then the depth of the canonical decision tree for $f$ under $\rho$ is at least the decision-tree depth of $f|_\rho$; that is, the least depth of any decision tree computing $f|_\rho$ does not exceed the depth of the canonical tree.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
ρ is a restriction on n variables
replaced:
The depth of the canonical decision tree for $f|_\rho$ is at least the decision-tree depth of the
restricted function: $(\mathrm{canonicalDTree}\,f\,\rho).\mathrm{depth} \ge \mathrm{dtDepth}\,(\mathrm{restrictFn}\,(f.\mathrm{eval})\,\rho)$.
